Hi Elena / NovaCorp procurement team —

Thanks for the clear asks. Below is a concise, auditable mapping we recommend for the RFP appendix. I've kept the language non-legal (so your counsel can easily lift it) and included worked examples using the telemetry you shared. Attaching an XLSX that has the same calculations so you can drop numbers in.

1) Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) — translation and example - Definition: Compute latency percentiles across all successful inference responses within the SLA window (UTC calendar month), excluding synthetic probes and canceled requests. - Calculation: Sort latency samples ascending; pX = value at (X/100 * N) rounding up index. - Worked example (from your telemetry sample): N = 10,000 requests; p95 index = ceil(0.95 * 10000) = 9500. If the 9500th sample = 312 ms, p95 = 312 ms.

2) Availability (uptime) — translation and example - Definition: Availability is the percentage of successful inferences served over total attempts during the SLA month, where successful is defined as a 2xx response from our runtime and completion of model generation (no gateway or internal 5xx). Periodic scheduled maintenance windows (pre-notified per contract) are excluded. - Calculation: availability = (successful_requests / total_requests) * 100 - Worked example: total_requests = 2,400,000; successful = 2,394,000 -> availability = (2,394,000 / 2,400,000) *100 = 99.75%

3) Cross-region weighting (multi-region endpoints) - Principle: We compute regional percentiles independently then report a weighted global percentile where weights are proportional to request counts by region for the month. This preserves customer-observed experience while avoiding bias from low-volume regions. - Calculation: For each region r, compute p95_r. Global weighted p95 = value such that sum_over_regions(weight_r * indicator(sample <= value)) >= 0.95 * total_weight. Practically we approximate by merging region histograms and applying request-count weights. - Worked example: US: 1,800,000 reqs p95=300ms; EU: 400,000 reqs p95=420ms. Merge weighted distribution => global p95 falls near the US tail but will be between 300–420ms depending on distribution; we would provide histograms in the evidence bundle.

4) Service credit calculation (monthly) — policy & sample arithmetic - Policy summary (proposed): If monthly availability < 99.9% and >= 99.0% -> 5% service credit; <99.0% and >= 95.0% -> 15% credit; <95.0% -> 50% credit. Credits are applied to the monthly invoice for the affected service and do not exceed the month's invoice amount. - Sample calc: If monthly invoice = $120,000 and observed availability = 99.75% -> falls in 99.0%–99.9% => 5% credit => credit = $6,000.

5) Edge cases & measurement hygiene (short bullets for RFP appendix) - Clock sync: All telemetry timestamps normalized to UTC using NTP-synced hosts. - Retry handling: Retries by clients are counted as separate attempts; internal transparent retries (e.g., silent workload resubmission in a canary fallback) are de-duplicated by request ID if present. - Partial responses: If model returns a truncated but 2xx response flagged as 'incomplete' in trace, it is classified as failed for availability. - Synthetic probes: Synthetic probes are ingested into separate telemetry partitions and excluded from SLA calculations; we include synthetic probe results as a separate observability indicator.

Attachments: SLA_Metric_Mapping.xlsx (detailed cells), telemetry-sample.json (your sample with annotations).

Elena, Aditya —

This looks good. Two small clarifications for the legal appendix that will help procurement avoid follow-ups: 1) specify the exact percentile interpolation rule we will use when N*X is non-integer (we recommend the nearest-rank method for auditability), and 2) call out the maximum evidence package turnaround (we can commit to 10 business days to provide raw telemetry and histogram artifacts for audits).

Suggested sentence for the appendix: "Percentile values are calculated using the nearest-rank method (index = ceil(p/100 * N)); in cases where customers request alternative statistical methods (e.g., linear interpolation), Redwood will provide both calculations as part of the evidence package but the nearest-rank value shall be used for contractual compliance unless otherwise mutually agreed in writing."

Monica — can you confirm we can commit to 10 business days for telemetry handoff (secure S3/Drive export with signed access)? If yes I will incorporate this sentence and finalize the text for Elena.

-Grace

Grace O'Connor
Principal, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
